implementationNotes: The three Chapter III additions also occur in the published PODC 2026 paper. They are indexed once under gen-bdgpsw26, with source links to published PDF pages 5, 6 and 10 and thesis theorem references.
The genus distance-k bound is an explicit thesis consequence: Meta-Theorem I gives 3α(k)+1 with α(k)=k^{O(k)}, hence k^{O(k)}, with parameter-dependent rounds f(g,k).
The path-excluded exact algorithm is attributed as folklore, with a componentwise construction and proof. No round-tightness claim is made.

The broader factor-50 point has its own excluded-H-uniform SOTA annotation. It does not automatically remove the K2t point or inherit its restricted t-domain SOTA certificate; full runtime functions remain uncompared.
Chapter IX remains work in progress; conjectures and the ambiguous X.2.2/X.2.3 statements are not indexed as proved bounds. Author clarification was requested for the latter.
The adaptive IV.3.3 statement has an apparent c(1) versus c(d) inconsistency and input-dependent minor parameter. It was not added as a universal 50 or a universal constant-round bound.
The LW24 cited result was already indexed in its full distance-k form; no duplicate article-specific k=1 row was added.
New sourced graph inclusions are used by the existing generic query engine. No paper IDs were hard-coded into filtering or derivation.

paper.title: Local Computation: Lower and Upper Bounds
paper.authors: Fabian Kuhn; Thomas Moscibroda; Roger Wattenhofer
paper.venue: Journal of the ACM 63(2), Article 17, pp. 1–44
paper.notes: Checked against arXiv v2 (31 March 2016); the primary preprint has 48 PDF pages. Lower bounds allow randomized algorithms and apply to expected approximation for a fixed round budget. References in Picavet thesis, Chapters I and IV.

suggestedResults.rounds: Ω(min{√(log n / log log n), log Δ / log log Δ})
suggestedResults.parameters: n is the number of vertices; Δ is the maximum degree. Polynomial-logarithmic exponents are fixed.
suggestedResults.assumptions: Also applies to deterministic algorithms. Randomized lower bound concerns expected approximation with a fixed worst-case round budget. There are hard graph families; n and Δ are coupled by the construction, so this is not a guarantee for every independently prescribed pair (n, Δ).
suggestedResults.summary: The primary result bounds the achievable expected ratio in r rounds by Ω(n^((1−o(1))/(4r²))/r) and Ω(Δ^(1/(r+1))/r). The combined n/Δ summary uses the minimum; no universal lower bound for each arbitrary independent parameter pair is inferred. Identifiers may be 1,…,n and nodes may know n, Δ and the unlabelled network topology.

suggestedResults.theorem: Theorem 15 and Corollary 16 (arXiv v2, PDF pp.21–23)
suggestedResults.summary: The minimum-dominating-set lower bound follows via a locality-preserving line-graph reduction from vertex cover. The primary r-round ratio tradeoff is Ω(n^((1−o(1))/(4r²))/r) and Ω(Δ^(1/(r+1))/r). The following remark explicitly extends this hardness to fractional MDS; that extension should use its own verified problem scope rather than ordinary integral-to-fractional inference.

suggestedResults.parameters: Fixed depth-one density bound ρ ≥ 1. The algorithm need not know ρ.
suggestedResults.assumptions: Port numbering; each node initially knows its incident ports. Messages have at most ⌈log Δ⌉ bits. This is the k=1 specialization of the already indexed distance-k algorithm, not a new theorem.
suggestedResults.summary: Substituting k=1 and f(1)=ρ gives O(1+√ρ) for ordinary MDS in exactly three rounds. Depth-one density is the largest edge-to-vertex ratio of a depth-one minor. Connected components may alternatively be processed independently if connectivity is dropped explicitly after review.
